features.name: duration_log
features.description: Log-transformed call duration to compress right skew and create better split points for tree models
features.expected_model_benefit: Nonlinear transformation allows tree to find meaningful thresholds in compressed duration space

features.name: previously_contacted
features.description: Binary indicator whether client was contacted in a previous campaign (pdays < 999 means they were contacted)
features.expected_model_benefit: Direct boolean split on prior contact history which strongly differentiates subscription likelihood

features.name: campaign_contact_burden
features.description: Ordinal bucket of campaign contacts: 1=single, 2=low(2-3), 3=medium(4-6), 4=high(7+) indicating contact fatigue
features.expected_model_benefit: Ordinal encoding of contact frequency allows tree to split on fatigue thresholds directly

features.name: economic_stress_index
features.description: Combined economic stress signal: high euribor3m and high employment rate suggest unfavorable economic conditions
features.expected_model_benefit: Interaction between interest rates and employment captures economic regime that affects subscription decisions

features.name: age_bucket
features.expected_model_benefit: Life-stage grouping captures nonlinear age effects on financial product subscription behavior

features.name: prior_success_indicator
features.description: Binary flag for successful previous campaign outcome (poutcome == 1 typically encodes success)
features.expected_model_benefit: Prior campaign success is a strong predictor; direct boolean split maximizes information gain

features.name: financial_risk_score
features.description: Composite financial risk: penalizes credit default and active loans, rewards no debt obligations
features.expected_model_benefit: Aggregated debt burden score provides a single split point capturing multiple financial risk dimensions

features.name: consumer_confidence_bucket
features.description: Consumer confidence index bucketed into 3 levels: 0=very_low(<-45), 1=moderate(-45 to -35), 2=high(>-35)
features.expected_model_benefit: Ordinal bucketing of consumer sentiment allows tree to split on sentiment regimes affecting financial decisions

features.name: call_duration_campaign_ratio
features.description: Average call duration per campaign contact, indicating engagement quality per contact attempt
features.expected_model_benefit: Normalizes duration by contact frequency to capture per-contact engagement quality for tree splits

features.name: high_education_professional
features.description: Binary indicator for high-education professionals: education >= 5 (university or higher) combined with professional job categories (job in 1,2,3,4)
features.expected_model_benefit: Interaction between education and job type captures high-value customer segment likely to subscribe

features.name: recency_engagement_score
features.description: Semantic score (0-3) assessing recency and depth of prior engagement: 0=never contacted, 1=contacted long ago with no follow-up, 2=recently contacted with some previous contacts, 3=recently contacted with multiple previous contacts indicating warm lead
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the combined recency and depth of prior relationship which tree can split on to identify warm leads

features.name: macroeconomic_favorability
features.description: Semantic score (0-3) assessing overall macroeconomic environment favorability for term deposit subscription: considers employment variation rate, consumer price index deviation from mean (93.58), and euribor3m level; 0=very unfavorable (high rates, poor employment), 3=very favorable (low rates, stable employment)
features.expected_model_benefit: Holistic economic regime indicator that tree can use as a high-level split to separate favorable vs unfavorable subscription environments
